text: The single most useful tool for ACL troubleshooting is the Security Debugger, sometimes called Debug Security Rules, reachable as a toggle in the user's profile menu or through System Diagnostics. Switch it on, reload the exact page in question, and it shows a security log underneath the output listing every single ACL the platform evaluated for that page, in order, with a clear pass or fail and the specific reason for each one.

This completely replaces the old guess-and-check approach of opening the Access Control list, filtering by table, and manually reasoning through every record that might apply. With the debugger switched on, you load the exact page the affected user is complaining about, and it hands you the real evaluation trace, the very same AND chain described back in an earlier lesson, happening live in front of you instead of purely in theory.

Editing an ACL is itself governed by ACLs. The sys_security_acl table has its own access rules, and by default even a full admin doesn't automatically bypass them. To edit ACL records, an admin needs the security_admin role active, and that role gets turned on through Elevate Roles under the profile icon, not held permanently switched on in the background.

This is deliberate design, never an oversight. Security_admin is powerful enough to bypass the very ACL script evaluation it's meant to configure. If it were always active, an admin editing some unrelated ACL could accidentally break the very ACL that governs ACL editing itself, with absolutely no safety net catching that mistake. Requiring a deliberate elevation step keeps that bypass power scoped to the one session where it's genuinely needed.

So the repeatable order of operations: identify the exact operation and field first, turn on the Security Debugger and reproduce the issue, open the specific ACL it flagged and check every ingredient, confirm the user's actual roles and group memberships rather than assuming, and only elevate roles when you actually need to edit the ACL record itself to fix it.
